34: ---
35:
36: ## 0. Fast path: no domain, stable URLs
37:
38: If the goal is to see the Activity actually work before renting a VPS, skip to
39: [Run everything locally](#6-run-everything-locally-no-domain). It needs no
40: domain and no VPS. Two hostnames never change:
41:
42: | Piece | Stable hostname |
43: | --- | --- |
44: | Viewer (static) | `https://streamy-viewer.pages.dev` |
45: | `/api` and `/relay` | `https://streamy-signal.thenightserver.workers.dev` |
46:
47: The Worker is a front door for this PC: it reads the current Cloudflare quick
48: tunnel hostname from a Durable Object and forwards `/token`, `/api/*` and the
49: relay WebSocket to it. `dev\start-activity.ps1` publishes the new tunnel
50: hostname to the Worker on every start, so the Developer Portal is filled in
51: **once** and never edited again. The tunnel hostname becomes an internal detail.
52:
53: The rest of this document describes the production shape: Pages, a public relay
54: and a public bot, each on its own hostname.
55:
56:
57: ---
58:
59: ## 1. Deploy the viewer to Cloudflare Pages
60:
61: The viewer is a Vite app and builds to a static `dist/`.
62:
63: `powershell
64: cd stream-site/viewer
65: npm install
66: # edit public/config.json first (see below)
67: npm run deploy
68: `
69:
70: `public/config.json` is copied into `dist/` and fetched at runtime:
71:
72: `json
73: {
74:   "signalURL": "wss://streamy-signal.thenightserver.workers.dev",
75:   "relayURL": "wss://relay.example.com",
76:   "tokenURL": "/.proxy/api/token",
77:   "discordClientID": "1539962249718792203"
78: }
79: `
80:
81: | Field | Purpose |
82: | --- | --- |
83: | `signalURL` | Existing Cloudflare signaling Worker (browser WebRTC lobby). |
84: | `relayURL` | Public relay host for **browser** relay testing (`?relay=<channel-id>`). Activity mode ignores it and uses the proxy path. |
85: | `tokenURL` | Relative Activity token endpoint. Must start with `/.proxy/`; Discord rewrites it. |
86: | `discordClientID` | Discord application (client) ID. Public, not a secret. |
87:
88: The build uses relative asset paths (`base: "./"`), so the same `dist/` works at
89: the Pages root and through the Discord proxy.
90:
91: ---
92:
93: ## 2. Deploy the relay
94:
95: The relay is a standalone Go module. It needs a publicly reachable **TLS**
96: endpoint; browser WebSockets from a `https:` Activity must use `wss:`.
97:
98: `bash
99: cd stream-site/relay
100: go build -o streamy-relay .
101: RELAY_PUBLISH_TOKEN='<long-random-secret>' ./streamy-relay -addr :8790 -max-viewers 200
102: `
103:
104: | Flag / env | Meaning |
105: | --- | --- |
106: | `-addr` | Listen address, default `:8790`. |
107: | `-publish-token` / `RELAY_PUBLISH_TOKEN` | Deployment-wide publisher secret. Empty disables publisher auth. |
108: | `-max-viewers` | Per-room viewer cap, default `200`; `0` is unlimited. |
109:
110: Put it behind Caddy, nginx, or another TLS terminator. Caddy handles WebSocket
111: upgrades automatically:
112:
113: `caddyfile
114: relay.example.com {
115:     reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8790
116: }
117: `
118:
119: For nginx, forward the upgrade headers:
120:
121: `nginx
122: location / {
123:     proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8790;
124:     proxy_http_version 1.1;
125:     proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
126:     proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
127:     proxy_read_timeout 300s;
128: }
129: `
130:
131: Check `https://relay.example.com/healthz` returns `ok`. The relay routes are
132: `/v1/publish/<room>` and `/v1/watch/<room>`; run it at the host root, not under a
133: path prefix. Publisher URLs configured in Streamy are base URLs such as
134: `wss://relay.example.com`.
135:
136: The relay keeps rooms in memory. It is a **single instance** design: restarting
137: it drops every stream, and it does not scale horizontally without sticky routing
138: per room.
139:
140: ---
141:
142: ## 3. Create the Discord application and Activity
143:
144: In the [Discord Developer Portal](https://discord.com/developers/applications):
145:
146: 1. **General Information** — copy the Application ID (client ID) and public key.
147: Under **OAuth2**, copy the Client Secret and add a placeholder redirect URI
148: such as `https://127.0.0.1`. The Embedded App SDK handles the real redirect;
149: the portal only requires that one exists.
150: 2. **Installation** — enable **Guild Install** (and optionally **User Install**).
151: The bot needs the `bot` and `applications.commands` scopes.
152: 3. **Activities → Getting Started** — enable Activities and set the Activity URL
153: to the Pages deployment, e.g. `https://streamy-viewer.pages.dev/`. Discord
154: loads that app through `https://<client-id>.discordsays.com/`.
155: 4. **Activities → URL Mappings** — add exactly these rows. The prefix is
156: **stripped** before the request reaches the target.
157:
158: | Prefix | Target (no protocol, no path) | What the Activity sends | What the target receives |
159: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
160: | `/api` | `streamy-signal.thenightserver.workers.dev` | `POST /.proxy/api/token` | `POST https://<current tunnel>/token` (via the Worker) |
161: | `/relay` | `streamy-signal.thenightserver.workers.dev` | `wss://<client-id>.discordsays.com/.proxy/relay/v1/watch/<room>` | `wss://<current tunnel>/v1/watch/<room>` (via the Worker) |
162:
163: Both rows point at the Worker, which forwards to whatever quick tunnel the
164: launcher published, so the mapping never changes. No `/` mapping is needed while
165: the Activity URL is the Pages deployment; add `/` → the Worker only if you also
166: want the Worker to serve the viewer.
167:
168: For a fully self-hosted deployment (Pages + a VPS relay + a public bot), use
169: `bot.example.com` and `relay.example.com` in those two rows instead, and add
170: `/` → `streamy-viewer.pages.dev`.
171:
172: Rules that matter:
173:
174: - Targets are hostnames only. Do **not** enter `https://` or `wss://`.
175: - List longer prefixes first; Discord matches on the longest prefix.
176: - `/.proxy/...` remains supported even though Discord now also accepts the
177: unprefixed path. Streamy uses `/.proxy/...` for backwards compatibility.
178: - The bot therefore listens on both `/token` (proxied) and `/api/token`
179: (direct). The desktop app notifies `https://bot.example.com/api/notify`.
180:
181: ### Entry Point command
182:
183: Under **Activities → Getting Started**, set the Entry Point command to the same
184: name the bot registers (`watch` by default). The bot creates `/watch` on startup
185: if it does not exist. If you change `ENTRY_COMMAND_NAME`, also change the Entry
186: Point command name in the portal.
187:
188: The bot handles **all** chat-input commands by returning callback type `12`, so
189: `/watch`, the Watch button, and a separately configured Entry Point command all
190: launch the same Activity. Do not register a second conflicting command.
191:
192: ### Install the bot
193:
194: Use the OAuth2 URL generator with scopes `bot` and `applications.commands`, and
195: the minimum permissions **View Channels** and **Send Messages** (3072). Install
196: it in the guild that will host streams. The bot does not need Administrator, and
197: it never automates a user account.
198:
199: ---
200:
201: ## 4. Run the bot
202:
203: The bot reads `bot/.env` on startup (real environment variables win), so the
204: shortest path is:
205:
206: `powershell
207: cd stream-site/bot
208: Copy-Item .env.example .env   # then edit the four required values
209: npm install
210: node src/index.js
211: `
212:
213: `node src/index.js` fails fast and names the missing variable if any of
214: `DISCORD_TOKEN`, `DISCORD_CLIENT_ID`, `DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET` or
215: `STREAMY_API_KEY` is empty. The equivalent explicit form:
216:
217: `bash
218: cd stream-site/bot
219: npm install
220: DISCORD_TOKEN='...' \
221: DISCORD_CLIENT_ID='...' \
222: DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET='...' \
223: STREAMY_API_KEY='<long-random-secret>' \
224: GUILD_ID='<optional-guild-id>' \
225: WATCH_CHANNEL_ID='<optional-default-channel-id>' \
226: ENTRY_COMMAND_NAME='watch' \
227: PORT=8791 \
228: node src/index.js
229: `
230:
231: | Variable | Meaning |
232: | --- | --- |
233: | `DISCORD_TOKEN` | Bot token. Never ship it in the viewer or desktop app. |
234: | `DISCORD_CLIENT_ID` | Application ID; used for the OAuth2 token exchange. |
235: | `DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET` | OAuth2 secret; server-side only. |
236: | `STREAMY_API_KEY` | Bearer token the desktop app uses for `/api/notify`. |
237: | `GUILD_ID` | Optional. Registers `/watch` in one guild immediately; global commands can take time to propagate. |
238: | `WATCH_CHANNEL_ID` | Optional default channel when a notify body has no `channelId`. |
239: | `ENTRY_COMMAND_NAME` | Command name, default `watch`. |
240: | `PORT` | HTTP API port, default `8791`, bound to loopback. |
241: | `TLS_CERT` / `TLS_KEY` | Optional direct TLS. Usually terminate TLS in Caddy instead. |
242:
243: Expose the bot over HTTPS so both Discord's proxy and the desktop app can reach
244: it:
245:
246: `caddyfile
247: bot.example.com {
248:     reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8791
249: }
250: `
251:
252: `POST /api/notify` requires `Authorization: Bearer $STREAMY_API_KEY`. It posts a
253: message with a **Watch** button in the target channel. The button's custom ID
254: always returns `LAUNCH_ACTIVITY`; it does not send a normal component reply.
255:
256: ---
257:
258: ## 5. Configure the desktop app
259:
260: Open **Settings → Discord Activity** (or edit `%AppData%\streamy\config.json`):
261:
262: `json
263: {
264:   "stream": {
265:     "relay": {
266:       "enabled": true,
267:       "url": "wss://relay.example.com",
268:       "token": "<RELAY_PUBLISH_TOKEN>",
269:       "channelID": "123456789012345678",
270:       "only": false,
271:       "notifyURL": "https://bot.example.com/api/notify",
272:       "notifyKey": "<STREAMY_API_KEY>"
273:     }
274:   }
275: }
276: `
277:
278: - **Enabled** turns the publisher on. With `only: false`, WebRTC and the browser
279: lobby still run.
280: - **Only** skips signaling and WebRTC. No viewer link is created; the stream is
281: Activity-only.
282: - **Channel ID** becomes the relay room. It must be the channel where viewers
283: will launch the Activity. The current desktop app uses one channel per stream;
284: changing channels requires changing this setting before starting.
285: - **Notify** is optional. If set, the app calls the bot once at stream start; a
286: failure is logged but does not stop the stream.
287: - Both URLs must be absolute `ws`/`wss` or `http`/`https` URLs. The relay base
288: URL must not contain a path.
289:
290: Settings apply to the **next** stream. Start sharing with the tray or hotkey.
291:
292: ---
293:
294: ## 6. Run everything locally (no domain)
295:
296: This is the fastest way to see the real Discord proxy, the real Activity SDK and
297: the real relay working together. Everything runs on this PC; the Activity talks
298: to the Worker, and the Worker talks to one Cloudflare quick tunnel.
299:
300: `301: Discord client
302:    │  https://streamy-viewer.pages.dev            static viewer (never changes)
303:    │      /.proxy/api/*   ─┐
304:    │      /.proxy/relay/* ─┤
305:    ▼                       ▼
306: https://streamy-signal.thenightserver.workers.dev  Worker (never changes)
307:    │  reads the current tunnel host from a Durable Object
308:    ▼
309: https://<random>.trycloudflare.com                 quick tunnel (changes every start)
310:    ▼
311: gateway :8799 ──┬── /            viewer/dist (local browser check)
312:                 ├── /v1, /relay  relay    :8790  ◀── desktop app (ws://127.0.0.1:8790)
313:                 └── /token, /api bot      :8791  ◀── desktop app (/api/notify)
314:`
315:
316: ### 6.1 One-time setup
317:
318: 1. **Fill in the bot secrets.** Create `bot/.env` (the launcher does this for you
319: on first run and then stops) and set `DISCORD_TOKEN`, `DISCORD_CLIENT_ID`,
320: `DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET` and any long random `STREAMY_API_KEY`.
321: 2. **Match the client ID.** `viewer/public/config.json` `discordClientID` must
322: equal `DISCORD_CLIENT_ID`. The launcher warns if they differ.
323: 3. **Deploy the Worker front door** (already done on this machine; repeat if you
324: clone the repo somewhere else):
325:
326: `powershell
327:    cd stream-site\worker
328:    npm install
329:    # one shared secret that lets the launcher publish the tunnel hostname
330:    npx wrangler secret put TUNNEL_ADMIN_TOKEN
331:    npx wrangler deploy
332:    `
333:
334: Keep the same value in `dev\secrets\tunnel-admin-token.txt` (one line, no
335: quotes). The launcher reads that file.
336: 4. **Deploy the viewer** so `https://streamy-viewer.pages.dev` serves the
337: Activity-aware build:
338:
339: `powershell
340:    cd stream-site\viewer
341:    npm run deploy
342:    `
343:
344: This builds `dist/` and uploads it. Deploy `dist/`, not `viewer/`: the source
345: page loads `/src/main.js`, so Discord cannot resolve the SDK's bare import.
346: 5. **Enable Activities for the app** in the Developer Portal.
347:
348: ### 6.2 Start the stack
349:
350: The desktop app starts the stack for you when **Start relay, bot and gateway
351: with Streamy** is enabled in **Settings → Discord Activity**, and stops it when
352: Streamy quits. Workers use `-Hidden`, so no extra terminals appear.
353:
354: To run it by hand instead:
355:
356: `powershell
357: cd stream-site
358: .\dev\start-activity.ps1                      # or: -PublishToken 'long-random-secret'
359: `
360:
361: The script builds the gateway, opens the relay, bot and gateway in three windows,
362: waits for their health endpoints, opens the quick tunnel, then publishes the
363: tunnel hostname to the Worker and prints:
364:
365: `366:   Tunnel (internal)      : https://random-words-1234.trycloudflare.com
367:   Stable Activity URL    : https://streamy-viewer.pages.dev/
368:   Stable mapping target  : https://streamy-signal.thenightserver.workers.dev
369: 
370:   Developer Portal -> Activities -> URL Mappings (set once):
371:     prefix  /api     target  streamy-signal.thenightserver.workers.dev
372:     prefix  /relay   target  streamy-signal.thenightserver.workers.dev
373: 
374:   Nothing to change after a restart - the tunnel hostname is published above.
375:`
376:
377: On first run only, set the developer portal to those values (see
378: [§3](#3-create-the-discord-application-and-activity)); after that a restart
379: changes nothing.
380:
381: Stop everything with:
382:
383: `powershell
384: .\dev\start-activity.ps1 -Stop
385: `
386:
387: `-Stop` also tells the Worker the relay is gone, so the Activity shows "relay
388: offline" instead of waiting on a dead tunnel. `-NoTunnel` runs the same stack for
389: a purely local browser check at `http://127.0.0.1:8799/`; `-NoPublish` skips the
390: Worker update.
391:
392: ### 6.3 Point the desktop app at the local stack
393:
394: Either fill in **Settings → Discord Activity**, or let the script write the
395: `stream.relay` block for you (it keeps a `config.json.bak` and reads the notify
396: key from `bot/.env`, so the two sides cannot drift):
397:
398: `powershell
399: .\dev\configure-desktop.ps1 -ChannelID <discord-channel-id>
400: # add -KeepWebRTC to keep WebRTC and the Activity at the same time (default)
401: `
402:
403: Restart `streamy.exe` afterwards; it reads the config at startup. The equivalent
404: settings are:
405:
406: | Setting | Value |
407: | --- | --- |
408: | Enabled | on |
409: | Relay URL | `ws://127.0.0.1:8790` |
410: | Publish token | whatever you passed as `-PublishToken` (default `devsecret`) |
411: | Channel ID | fallback text channel — right-click it with Developer Mode on → Copy Channel ID. When you are connected to a voice channel, the bot uses that voice channel instead |
412: | Relay only | off — keeps WebRTC and the Pages lobby working; turn on only to test the relay in isolation |
413: | Notify URL | `http://127.0.0.1:8791/api/notify` |
414: | Notify key | the `STREAMY_API_KEY` from `bot/.env` |
415:
416: The room is exactly `channelID` — or the streamer's current voice channel when
417: one is available. The desktop app asks the bot for that channel before it starts
418: publishing, and the Activity joins the room of the channel it was launched from,
419: so a mismatch is the most common "waiting forever" cause.
420:
421: ### 6.4 Launch the Activity
422:
423: 1. Invite the bot to a test server (scopes `bot` + `applications.commands`).
424: 2. Join a voice channel if you want the Activity there. Start sharing (`Ctrl+\`).
425: The relay window should log the publisher, and the bot should post a Watch
426: message in your voice channel (otherwise in the fallback channel).
427: 3. Click **Watch** (or run `/watch`; if you are in voice, the bot puts the
428: button in the voice channel's text chat). Discord opens the Activity, the
429: viewer completes `ready()` / `authorize()` / token exchange and joins the
430: room of that channel. Stopping the stream removes the Watch invite.
431: 4. Watch the gateway window: `POST /token -> 200` and
432: `GET /v1/watch/<channel-id> -> 200 (websocket)` mean the proxy is working. A
433: `502` means the bot is down; a viewer that connects but stays black means no
434: publisher in that room.
435:
436: Restarting this PC or the stack only changes the tunnel hostname, and the
437: launcher republishes it to the Worker automatically. The Developer Portal keeps
438: pointing at `streamy-viewer.pages.dev` and `streamy-signal.thenightserver.workers.dev`
439: for good.
440:
441: Quick sanity check without Discord (browser WebRTC/relay path, needs
442: `relayURL` in `viewer/public/config.json` to point at a public relay):
443:
444: `powershell
445: # The room must match stream.relay.channelID.
446: # https://streamy-viewer.pages.dev/?relay=123456789012345678
447: `
448:
449: ### 6.5 If you do have separate hosts
450:
451: With Pages, a VPS relay and a public bot you can tunnel each port separately
452: instead of using the gateway:
453:
454: 1. `cd stream-site/viewer; npm run build; npm run preview -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8787`
455: then `cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8787`.
456: 2. Start the relay (`go run . -addr :8790`) and tunnel port 8790.
457: 3. Start the bot (`node src/index.js`) and tunnel port 8791.
458: 4. Point `/`, `/api` and `/relay` at the three tunnel hostnames and set the
459: Activity URL to the viewer tunnel host.
460:
461: Do not use the Activity URL Override for this test. Discord documents that an
462: override bypasses its proxy, so `/.proxy/...` requests will not be rewritten.
463: Launch through the normal Activity entry point instead.
464:
465: ---
466:
467: ## 7. Test plan (browser and Activity simultaneously)
468:
469: Prerequisites: ffmpeg installed, the viewer deployed, the relay and bot running,
470: and at least one guild where the bot is installed. For a two-viewer test, use two
471: Discord accounts in the same channel.
472:
473: 1. **WebRTC baseline** — start a stream with relay enabled but not relay-only.
474: Open the normal viewer link in Chrome and confirm video, audio after unmute,
475: and a `Live` status.
476: 2. **Activity launch** — click the bot's **Watch** button. The Activity opens,
477: runs `ready()` / `authorize()` / token exchange, and joins room
478: `<channel-id>`. Confirm video appears without a manual reconnect.
479: 3. **Simultaneous viewers** — keep the browser viewer open and launch the
480: Activity in a second Discord client. Both should play the same stream. Relay
481: logs should show two viewers, and viewer egress should be roughly twice the
482: publisher ingress.
483: 4. **Relay-only** — enable `stream.relay.only`, restart sharing, and confirm the
484: browser lobby no longer lists the stream while the Activity still works.
485: Disable it again and confirm WebRTC returns.
486: 5. **Per-viewer launch** — have a second user run `/watch` (or click the button)
487: themselves. One user launching must not push the Activity to anyone else.
488: 6. **Publisher restart** — stop sharing while the Activity is open. The viewer
489: gets close code `4001` and waits. Start sharing again; it reconnects and
490: receives the cached keyframe without a page reload.
491: 7. **Keyframe/stale handling** — leave the Activity tab backgrounded for a
492: minute, then return. The viewer should resynchronize at the next IDR. Throttle
493: one viewer in DevTools; the relay should close it with `4004` and the viewer
494: should reconnect, while the other viewer and the publisher are unaffected.
495: 8. **Viewer cap** — run the relay with `-max-viewers 1` and connect a second
496: viewer. It should receive `4003` / "This stream is full" and retry later.
497: 9. **Audio/video sync** — unmute and watch a clock or counting video for ten
498: minutes. Check that audio stays aligned; the relay timestamps both streams on
499: the same Unix-millisecond clock.
500: 10. **Bot paths** — verify all three launch paths: the Watch button, `/watch`,
501: and the portal Entry Point command. Bot logs must not contain
502: `LAUNCH_ACTIVITY failed`.
503: 11. **Failure modes** — use a wrong relay token (stream start fails with "relay
504: rejected publisher"), a wrong bot key (HTTP 401, no message posted), and a
505: wrong channel ID (no message / viewer waits for a publisher).
506: 12. **Fallback** — test a browser without WebCodecs H.264 support. The viewer
507: should switch to the MSE compatibility player or report a clear error.
508:
509: ---
510:
511: ## 8. Known limits
512:
513: - **Latency is roughly 0.5–2 s.** Encode, relay buffering, jitter scheduling,
514: and decoder queues add up. This is fine for watching, not for competitive
515: play.
516: - **TCP head-of-line blocking.** The relay path is WebSocket over TCP. Packet
517: loss stalls every frame behind it; WebRTC's UDP path degrades more gracefully.
518: Expect visible freezes on a poor mobile connection.
519: - **Relay bandwidth is the real cost.** Publisher ingress is about the stream
520: bitrate; viewer egress is about `bitrate × viewers`. A 6 Mbps stream with 50
521: viewers needs ~300 Mbps of egress. Cap viewers and monitor the relay's
522: `relay bandwidth` log lines.
523: - **One relay instance, in-memory rooms.** Restarting drops all streams, and
524: there is no cross-instance routing. Run one instance per region or accept the
525: single point of failure.
526: - **One publisher and one configured channel per stream.** The room is the
527: Discord channel ID from config. Supporting several channels concurrently needs
528: one app instance (or a future channel picker) per channel.
529: - **The relay sees all media.** Unlike WebRTC, there is no end-to-end media path.
530: Treat the VPS and `RELAY_PUBLISH_TOKEN` as sensitive. The token is
531: deployment-wide, so anyone holding it can publish to any room.
532: - **Viewers are not authenticated.** The channel ID is the capability; anyone
533: who knows it and can reach the relay can watch. Keep the relay behind TLS and
534: do not publish room IDs.
535: - **Discord proxy limits.** Only mapped paths are reachable. Mappings strip the
536: prefix, targets omit the protocol, the root mapping must be last, and hosts
537: must use TLS. WebSockets are supported but are still subject to idle and
538: message-size limits.
539: - **Activities are launched per viewer.** Discord does not broadcast one user's
540: Activity to a channel. Every viewer clicks Watch or runs `/watch`. Bots may
541: not automate user accounts or act as self-bots; use the official bot token and
542: Activity SDK only.
543: - **Codec support varies.** WebCodecs H.264 is not universal. MSE fallback adds
544: latency, and Opus-in-MP4 audio support is not universal, in which case the
545: viewer plays video without sound.
546: - **Autoplay policy.** Viewers start muted; audio requires a user gesture. This
547: is enforced by browsers, especially on mobile.
548: - **No recording, DVR, or seek.** The relay is live-only and drops stale frames
549: instead of queueing them.
550: - **Discord ToS.** Do not self-bot, scrape, or automate a user account. The bot
551: must remain a normal bot application, and the Activity must use the official
552: Embedded App SDK.
553: - **Quick tunnels are for testing only.** The hostname is random and changes on
554: every restart. That no longer touches the Developer Portal (the Worker absorbs
555: it), but Cloudflare rate-limits quick tunnels and either end can be slow under
556: load. For an always-on relay with no Worker in the path, use a Cloudflare-managed
557: domain (named tunnel) or a VPS with a real certificate.
558: - **The Worker front door is a proxy, not a relay.** It forwards to the PC, so the
559: PC must be awake and the tunnel up. When the stack is stopped, `/token` and
560: `/relay` return `503 {"error":"relay-offline"}` instead of hanging.
561: - **The local stack is not always on.** The relay, bot and gateway run while
562: their windows are open; closing them, sleeping the PC or losing the network
563: ends every Activity stream.
564:
565: ---
566:
567: ## Troubleshooting
568:
569: | Symptom | Likely cause |
570: | --- | --- |
571: | Activity shows a blank page | The Activity URL does not serve `index.html` + `assets/` (check `https://streamy-viewer.pages.dev/`), or a `/` mapping exists and shadows the Activity URL. |
572: | `Failed to resolve module specifier "@discord/embedded-app-sdk"` | The Pages deployment is serving the viewer **source** instead of `dist/` (the HTML references `/src/main.js`). Run `npm run deploy` from `stream-site/viewer` and redeploy `dist/`. |
573: | `blocked:csp` / failed fetch | A backend URL was absolute or not under a mapped prefix. Use `/.proxy/...`. |
574: | Token exchange 502 | Wrong client ID/secret, expired code, or the bot cannot reach Discord. Check bot logs; the response now includes the upstream detail. |
575: | Token exchange 404 | The `/api` mapping points at a host that does not serve `/token`. The prefix is stripped. |
576: | Gateway returns 502 | The relay or bot is not running, or on a different port. The gateway logs the failing upstream URL; its `/healthz` shows the configured targets. |
577: | A `/token` failure shows Cloudflare's own "502 Bad gateway" page | Quick-tunnel edges replace origin 5xx bodies with their own error page. The bot's real message (`token exchange failed: …`) is in the bot window; `curl http://127.0.0.1:8791/token` shows it locally. Successful exchanges (200) are unaffected. |
578: | Worked, then broke after a restart | The tunnel hostname changed but the Worker was not updated. Run `.\dev\start-activity.ps1` again (it publishes the host), then check `GET /__tunnel` with the admin token. |
579: | `/token` or `/relay` returns 503 `relay-offline` | The Worker has no tunnel host: the stack is stopped, or the launcher could not publish. Resume with `.\dev\start-activity.ps1`. |
580: | `GET /__tunnel` is 401/503 | `TUNNEL_ADMIN_TOKEN` in the Worker does not match `dev\secrets\tunnel-admin-token.txt`, or the secret was never set. |
581: | Relay connection fails in Activity | `/relay` mapping missing, target not TLS, or the reverse proxy is not forwarding WebSocket upgrades. |
582: | Relay rejects publisher | `stream.relay.token` does not match `RELAY_PUBLISH_TOKEN`. |
583: | Viewer waits forever | No publisher in that room. Check that `stream.relay.channelID` equals the channel where the Activity was launched. |
584: | Watch button does nothing | Bot lacks permission in the channel, the Activity is not enabled, or `LAUNCH_ACTIVITY` failed. Check bot logs. |
585: | Video but no audio | The viewer is muted (autoplay), Opus/MP4 is unsupported, or desktop audio is disabled in Settings. |

123: // dialRelay opens a relay WebSocket through the gateway's /relay proxy,
124: // performing the role handshake the desktop app and the viewer use.
125: func dialRelay(t *testing.T, gatewayAddr, role, room, token string) (_websocket.Conn, func()) {
126: t.Helper()
127: segment := "watch"
128: if role == "publisher" {
129: segment = "publish"
130: }
131: url := "ws://" + gatewayAddr + "/.proxy/relay/v1/" + segment + "/" + room
132: conn, *, err := websocket.DefaultDialer.Dial(url, nil)
133: if err != nil {
134: t.Fatalf("dial %s: %v", role, err)
135: }
136:
137: hello := map[string]any{"v": protocol.ProtocolVersion, "type": "hello", "role": role, "token": token}
138: if err := conn.WriteJSON(hello); err != nil {
139: conn.Close()
140: t.Fatalf("%s hello: %v", role, err)
141: }
142: * = conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 _ time.Second))
143: var ready struct {
144: Type string `json:"type"`
145: Code string `json:"code"`
146: Role string `json:"role"`
147: Error string `json:"message"`
148: }
149: if err := conn.ReadJSON(&ready); err != nil {
150: conn.Close()
151: t.Fatalf("%s ready: %v", role, err)
152: }
153: if ready.Type != "ready" {
154: conn.Close()
155: t.Fatalf("%s was not accepted: %+v", role, ready)
156: }
157: if ready.Role != role {
158: conn.Close()
159: t.Fatalf("%s ready reported role %q", role, ready.Role)
160: }
161: _ = conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Time{})
162: return conn, func() { conn.Close() }
163: }

165: // readMedia returns the next binary media frame, failing on text messages or
166: // when the deadline passes.
167: func readMedia(t *testing.T, conn *websocket.Conn, within time.Duration) protocol.MediaFrame {
168: t.Helper()
169: _ = conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(within))
170: messageType, data, err := conn.ReadMessage()
171: if err != nil {
172: t.Fatalf("read media: %v", err)
173: }
174: if messageType != websocket.BinaryMessage {
175: t.Fatalf("expected a binary media frame, got message type %d: %s", messageType, data)
176: }
177: frame, err := protocol.ParseMediaFrame(data)
178: if err != nil {
179: t.Fatalf("parse media frame: %v", err)
180: }
181: return frame
182: }

184: // TestStreamFlowsThroughGateway is the end-to-end check for the Activity path:
185: // a publisher connects through the gateway proxy, a viewer connects through the
186: // same proxy, and the encoded H.264 and Opus frames reach the viewer.
187: func TestStreamFlowsThroughGateway(t _testing.T) {
188: stack := startStack(t)
189:
190: publisher, closePublisher := dialRelay(t, stack.gatewayAddr, "publisher", "room-1", "publish-token")
191: defer closePublisher()
192: viewer, closeViewer := dialRelay(t, stack.gatewayAddr, "viewer", "room-1", "")
193: defer closeViewer()
194:
195: // A real access unit is Annex-B: SPS, PPS and an IDR slice. The relay has
196: // to recognise it as a keyframe so a viewer that joins later gets it.
197: sps := []byte{0, 0, 0, 1, 0x67, 0x42, 0xE0, 0x1F}
198: pps := []byte{0, 0, 0, 1, 0x68, 0xCE, 0x3C, 0x80}
199: idr := []byte{0, 0, 0, 1, 0x65, 0x88, 0x84, 0x00}
200: keyframe := append(append(append([]byte(nil), sps...), pps...), idr...)
201:
202: if err := publisher.WriteMessage(websocket.BinaryMessage,
203: protocol.EncodeMediaFrame(protocol.MediaVideo, protocol.FlagKeyframe, 1000, keyframe)); err != nil {
204: t.Fatalf("publish keyframe: %v", err)
205: }
206: time.Sleep(100 _ time.Millisecond)
207:
208: // A viewer joining after the keyframe must receive the cached keyframe
209: // before any delta frame, or it cannot decode the stream.
210: cached := readMedia(t, viewer, 2*time.Second)
211: if cached.Kind != protocol.MediaVideo {
212: t.Fatalf("cached frame kind = %d, want video", cached.Kind)
213: }
214: if cached.Flags&protocol.FlagKeyframe == 0 {
215: t.Fatalf("cached frame was not marked as a keyframe")
216: }
217:
218: delta := []byte{0, 0, 0, 1, 0x41, 0x9A, 0x22}
219: if err := publisher.WriteMessage(websocket.BinaryMessage,
220: protocol.EncodeMediaFrame(protocol.MediaVideo, 0, 1033, delta)); err != nil {
221: t.Fatalf("publish delta: %v", err)
222: }
223: live := readMedia(t, viewer, 2*time.Second)
224: if live.Kind != protocol.MediaVideo || live.Timestamp != 1033 {
225: t.Fatalf("live frame = kind %d timestamp %d, want video at 1033", live.Kind, live.Timestamp)
226: }
227: if string(live.Payload) != string(delta) {
228: t.Fatalf("live payload = %x, want %x", live.Payload, delta)
229: }
230:
231: audio := []byte{0xDE, 0xAD, 0xBE, 0xEF}
232: if err := publisher.WriteMessage(websocket.BinaryMessage,
233: protocol.EncodeMediaFrame(protocol.MediaAudio, 0, 1040, audio)); err != nil {
234: t.Fatalf("publish audio: %v", err)
235: }
236: gotAudio := readMedia(t, viewer, 2*time.Second)
237: if gotAudio.Kind != protocol.MediaAudio {
238: t.Fatalf("audio frame kind = %d, want audio", gotAudio.Kind)
239: }
240: if string(gotAudio.Payload) != string(audio) {
241: t.Fatalf("audio payload = %x, want %x", gotAudio.Payload, audio)
242: }
243: }

4: Runs the whole Discord Activity stack on this PC behind one Cloudflare quick

8: Starts the relay, the bot and the gateway (viewer build + /api + /relay
9: proxies) in their own windows, then opens a quick tunnel in front of the
10: gateway. A free quick tunnel can only point at one port, which is exactly why
11: the gateway exists: one public origin serves the Activity, the token exchange

14: The quick tunnel hostname changes on every start, but the Discord Developer

16: streamy-signal Worker, and the portal mappings point at that Worker
17: (stable) plus the Pages deployment (stable).

24: The stable front door. Defaults to https://streamy-signal.thenightserver.workers.dev

128: // bot serves that prefix) and /.proxy/relay/x -> /v1/x (Discord strips
129: // /.proxy, and the relay serves /v1).
130: rest := strings.TrimPrefix(req.URL.Path, gatewayPrefix)
131: prefix := strings.TrimSuffix(upstreamPrefix, "/")
132: req.URL.Path = prefix + "/" + strings.TrimPrefix(rest, "/")
133: req.URL.RawPath = ""
134: }
135: // The prefix must only be removed here. Wrapping with http.StripPrefix
136: // would strip it twice and every proxied request would miss its segment.
137: return proxy

## Assistant

_Thinking:_

The bot's token exchange passes redirect_uri; for the Activity SDK flow, Discord expects no redirect_uri (the code came from `sdk.commands.authorize()`). Actually according to Discord docs, token exchange for Activity should include `grant_type=authorization_code`, `code`, and client credentials, with NO redirect_uri. So omit redirect_uri and make `expires_in` a number.

Also need CORS headers since Discord Activity iframe origin is `https://<clientid>.discordsays.com`; fetch to `/.proxy/api/token` is same-origin through the proxy, so CORS may not be strictly needed but harmless. Actually with `/.proxy/` the request is proxied through Discord's proxy, so same origin. But if viewer is served directly by Worker/tunnel, origin differs. Add Access-Control-Allow-Origin: \* with OPTIONS handling.

Note `strconv` import might become unused — check other uses of strconv in bot.go.

184: // TestStreamFlowsThroughGateway is the end-to-end check for the Activity path:
185: // a publisher connects through the gateway proxy, a viewer connects through the
186: // same proxy, and the encoded H.264 and Opus frames reach the viewer.
187: func TestStreamFlowsThroughGateway(t _testing.T) {

196: // to recognise it as a keyframe so a viewer that joins later gets it.
197: sps := []byte{0, 0, 0, 1, 0x67, 0x42, 0xE0, 0x1F}
198: pps := []byte{0, 0, 0, 1, 0x68, 0xCE, 0x3C, 0x80}
199: idr := []byte{0, 0, 0, 1, 0x65, 0x88, 0x84, 0x00}
200: keyframe := append(append(append([]byte(nil), sps...), pps...), idr...)
201:
202: if err := publisher.WriteMessage(websocket.BinaryMessage,
203: protocol.EncodeMediaFrame(protocol.MediaVideo, protocol.FlagKeyframe, 1000, keyframe)); err != nil {
204: t.Fatalf("publish keyframe: %v", err)
205: }
206: time.Sleep(100 _ time.Millisecond)
207:
208: // A viewer joining after the keyframe must receive the cached keyframe
209: // before any delta frame, or it cannot decode the stream.
210: cached := readMedia(t, viewer, 2*time.Second)
211: if cached.Kind != protocol.MediaVideo {
212: t.Fatalf("cached frame kind = %d, want video", cached.Kind)
213: }
214: if cached.Flags&protocol.FlagKeyframe == 0 {
215: t.Fatalf("cached frame was not marked as a keyframe")
216: }
217:
218: delta := []byte{0, 0, 0, 1, 0x41, 0x9A, 0x22}
219: if err := publisher.WriteMessage(websocket.BinaryMessage,
220: protocol.EncodeMediaFrame(protocol.MediaVideo, 0, 1033, delta)); err != nil {
221: t.Fatalf("publish delta: %v", err)
222: }
223: live := readMedia(t, viewer, 2*time.Second)
224: if live.Kind != protocol.MediaVideo || live.Timestamp != 1033 {
225: t.Fatalf("live frame = kind %d timestamp %d, want video at 1033", live.Kind, live.Timestamp)

227: if string(live.Payload) != string(delta) {

204: // deriveWorkerURL converts the signaling WebSocket URL to the Worker HTTP URL.
205: // e.g., wss://streamy-signal.thenightserver.workers.dev -> https://streamy-signal.thenightserver.workers.dev
206: func deriveWorkerURL(signalingURL string) string {
207: u, err := url.Parse(signalingURL)
208: if err != nil {
209: return ""
210: }
211: if u.Scheme == "wss" {
212: u.Scheme = "https"
213: return u.String()
214: }
215: if u.Scheme == "ws" {
216: u.Scheme = "http"
217: return u.String()
218: }
219: return signalingURL
220: }

309: // Start launches the child in the background. It is safe to call repeatedly.
310: func (m *Manager) Start() {
311: m.mu.Lock()
312: if m.started {
313: m.mu.Unlock()
314: return
315: }
316: m.started = true
317: m.generation++
318: generation := m.generation
319: script := m.script
320: m.mu.Unlock()
321:
322: if script != "" {
323: if info, err := os.Stat(script); err == nil && !info.IsDir() {
324: m.logger.Info("starting the local stack from a script", "script", script)
325: go m.runScript(script, generation)
326: return
327: }
328: m.logger.Warn("configured stack script was not found; using the built-in stack", "script", script)
329: }

331: // A previous Streamy process may have left the stack running. Adopt it
332: // instead of fighting over the port.
333: if m.healthOK() {
334: m.mu.Lock()
335: if generation == m.generation {
336: m.running = true
337: m.owned = false
338: m.err = nil
339: }
340: m.mu.Unlock()
341: m.logger.Info(m.label()+" is already running", "health", m.healthAddr)
342: return
343: }
344:
345: ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
346: done := make(chan struct{})
347: m.mu.Lock()
348: if generation != m.generation {
349: m.mu.Unlock()
350: cancel()
351: return
352: }
353: m.cancel = cancel
354: m.procDone = done
355: m.owned = true
356: m.mu.Unlock()

358: if m.mode == "activity" {

360: "gateway", m.gatewayAddr, "relay", m.relayAddr, "bot", m.botAddr)
361: go m.runChild(ctx, done, generation, m.activityArgs(), m.label())
362: return
363: }
364: go m.runChild(ctx, done, generation,
365: []string{"bot", "-port", strconv.Itoa(m.port)}, m.label())
366: }

439: // runChild starts args as a child of this executable and waits until its health
440: // endpoint answers. It is shared by the notification bot and the Activity
441: // stack so both get the same crash handling and startup timeout.
442: func (m *Manager) runChild(ctx context.Context, done chan struct{}, generation int, args []string, label string) {
443: defer close(done)
444:
445: self, err := m.self()
446: if err != nil {
447: m.finish(generation, err, false)
448: return
449: }
450: cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, self, args...)
451: cmd.Dir = filepath.Dir(self)
452: executil.HideConsoleWindow(cmd)
453:
454: // Pass Discord credentials as environment variables (activity command reads from env as fallback)
455: if m.discordClientID != "" {
456: cmd.Env = append(cmd.Env, "DISCORD_CLIENT_ID="+m.discordClientID)
457: }
458: if m.discordSecret != "" {
459: cmd.Env = append(cmd.Env, "DISCORD_CLIENT_SECRET="+m.discordSecret)
460: }
461: if m.identitySecret != "" {
462: cmd.Env = append(cmd.Env, "DISCORD_IDENTITY_SECRET="+m.identitySecret)
463: }
464: // Also pass publish token for the relay
465: if m.publishToken != "" {
466: cmd.Env = append(cmd.Env, "DISCORD_PUBLISH_TOKEN="+m.publishToken)
467: }
468:
469: if logFile := m.openLog(); logFile != nil {
470: cmd.Stdout = logFile
471: cmd.Stderr = logFile
472: defer logFile.Close()
473: }
474: if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
475: m.finish(generation, err, false)
476: return
477: }
478:
479: waitCh := make(chan error, 1)
480: go func() { waitCh <- cmd.Wait() }()
481:
482: deadline := time.Now().Add(startupTimeout)
483: ticker := time.NewTicker(250 * time.Millisecond)
484: defer ticker.Stop()
485: for {
486: select {
487: case err := <-waitCh:
488: // The child exited before it became healthy: a bad token, a port
489: // already in use, or a missing .env.
490: if err != nil {
491: m.logger.Warn(label+" exited during startup", "error", err)
492: }
493: m.finish(generation, err, false)
494: return
495: case <-ctx.Done():
496: * = cmd.Process.Kill()
497: <-waitCh
498: m.finish(generation, ctx.Err(), false)
499: return
500: case <-ticker.C:
501: if m.healthOK() {
502: m.mu.Lock()
503: if generation == m.generation {
504: m.running = true
505: m.err = nil
506: }
507: m.mu.Unlock()
508: m.logger.Info(label+" is ready", "health", m.healthAddr)
509:
510: err := <-waitCh
511: if err != nil && ctx.Err() == nil {
512: m.logger.Warn(label+" exited", "error", err)
513: }
514: m.finish(generation, err, false)
515: return
516: }
517: if time.Now().After(deadline) {
518: _ = cmd.Process.Kill()
519: <-waitCh
520: m.finish(generation, fmt.Errorf("%s did not become healthy on %s", label, m.healthAddr), false)
521: return
522: }
523: }
524: }
525: }

530: if generation != m.generation {
531: m.mu.Unlock()
532: cancel()
533: return
534: }

536: m.mu.Unlock()
537: defer cancel()

539: args := []string{"-NoProfile", "-ExecutionPolicy", "Bypass", "-File", script, "-Hidden"}
540: if m.publishToken != "" {
541: args = append(args, "-PublishToken", m.publishToken)
542: }
543: err := m.exec(ctx, args...)
544: m.finish(generation, err, err == nil)
545: if err != nil {

547: return
548: }
549: m.logger.Info("the local stack is ready")
550: }

552: func (m *Manager) finish(generation int, err error, running bool) {
553: m.mu.Lock()
554: defer m.mu.Unlock()
555: if generation != m.generation {
556: return
557: }
558: m.running = running
559: m.err = err
560: if !running {
561: // The child is gone. Clear started so the next Start (for example when
562: // the user begins a new stream) relaunches it instead of leaving the
563: // manager stuck after a failed startup or a crash.
564: m.started = false
565: m.owned = false
566: }
567: }

585: response, err := client.Get("http://" + m.healthAddr + "/healthz")
586: if err != nil {
587: return false

594: func (m *Manager) requestQuit(ctx context.Context) {
595: if m.apiKey == "" {
596: return
597: }
598: quitCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 2*time.Second)
599: defer cancel()
600: request, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(quitCtx, http.MethodPost,
601: fmt.Sprintf("http://127.0.0.1:%d/api/quit", m.port), nil)
602: if err != nil {
603: return

605: request.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+m.apiKey)
606: client := http.Client{Timeout: 2 * time.Second}
607: response, err := client.Do(request)
608: if err != nil {
609: return
610: }
611: response.Body.Close()
612: }

702: // localActivityAddresses decides whether the built-in Activity stack should run
703: // for this relay URL and, if so, which ports it should use. Only a plain ws URL
704: // on a loopback host can be served by the built-in plain-WebSocket stack; a
705: // remote or TLS relay is somebody else's deployment and must not spawn one.
706: //
707: // The port in the URL tells us which service the desktop app publishes to:
708: // ws://127.0.0.1:8080/.proxy/relay goes through the gateway, while
709: // ws://127.0.0.1:8081 talks to the relay directly.
710: func localActivityAddresses(enabled bool, raw string) (gateway, relay, bot string, ok bool) {
711: if !enabled {
712: return "", "", "", false
713: }
714: parsed, err := url.Parse(strings.TrimSpace(raw))
715: if err != nil || parsed.Scheme != "ws" {
716: return "", "", "", false
717: }
718: switch strings.ToLower(parsed.Hostname()) {
719: case "127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1":
720: default:
721: return "", "", "", false
722: }
723: portNumber, err := strconv.Atoi(parsed.Port())
724: if err != nil || portNumber < 1 || portNumber > 65535 {
725: return "", "", "", false
726: }
727:
728: used := map[int]bool{}
729: var gatewayPort, relayPort, botPort int
730: if strings.Contains(parsed.Path, "/.proxy/relay") {
731: gatewayPort = portNumber
732: used[gatewayPort] = true
733: relayPort = firstFreePort(used, defaultRelayPort, 18081)
734: botPort = firstFreePort(used, defaultActivityBotPort, 18083)
735: } else {
736: relayPort = portNumber
737: used[relayPort] = true
738: gatewayPort = firstFreePort(used, defaultGatewayPort, 18080)
739: botPort = firstFreePort(used, defaultActivityBotPort, 18083)
740: }
741: return fmt.Sprintf(":%d", gatewayPort),
742: fmt.Sprintf(":%d", relayPort),
743: fmt.Sprintf(":%d", botPort),
744: true
745: }
746:
747: // firstFreePort returns the first candidate port that is not already assigned
748: // to another service. The fallback list is deliberately short and predictable;
749: // a busy port still fails fast inside `streamy activity` with a clear error.
750: func firstFreePort(used map[int]bool, candidates ...int) int {
751: for _, port := range candidates {
752: if !used[port] {
753: used[port] = true
754: return port
755: }
756: }
757: for port := 28080; ; port++ {
758: if !used[port] {
759: used[port] = true
760: return port
761: }
762: }
763: }

765: // healthAddr turns a listen address into one that can be dialled locally.
766: func healthAddr(listen string) string {
767: host, port, err := net.SplitHostPort(listen)
768: if err != nil {
769: return "127.0.0.1" + listen
770: }
771: switch host {
772: case "", "::", "0.0.0.0":
773: host = "127.0.0.1"
774: }
775: return net.JoinHostPort(host, port)
776: }

778: func portFromNotifyURL(raw string) int {
779: if strings.TrimSpace(raw) == "" {
780: return defaultBotPort
781: }
782: parsed, err := url.Parse(raw)
783: if err != nil {
784: return defaultBotPort
785: }
786: if value := parsed.Port(); value != "" {
787: if port, err := strconv.Atoi(value); err == nil && port > 0 && port < 65536 {
788: return port
789: }
790: }
791: return defaultBotPort
792: }

// loadTunnelAdminToken reads the Worker admin secret from the stack directory.
func loadTunnelAdminToken(logDir string) string {
	if logDir == "" { return "" }
	data, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(logDir, "stack", "tunnel-admin-token.txt"))
	if err != nil { return "" }
	return strings.TrimSpace(string(data))
}

func saveTunnelAdminToken(logDir, token string, logger *slog.Logger) {

	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "tunnel-admin-token.txt"), []byte(token), 0o600); err != nil { ... }
}

#Requires -Version 5.1
<#
.SYNOPSIS
Runs the whole Discord Activity stack on this PC behind one Cloudflare quick
tunnel.

.DESCRIPTION
Starts the relay, the bot and the gateway (viewer build + /api + /relay
proxies) in their own windows, then opens a quick tunnel in front of the
gateway. A free quick tunnel can only point at one port, which is exactly why
the gateway exists: one public origin serves the Activity, the token exchange
and the WebSocket relay.

    The quick tunnel hostname changes on every start, but the Discord Developer
    Portal never sees it: this script publishes the current hostname to the
    streamy-signal Worker, and the portal mappings point at that Worker
    (stable) plus the Pages deployment (stable).

.PARAMETER Stop
Stops the processes listening on the relay, bot and gateway ports, kills the
quick tunnel started by this script, and tells the Worker the relay is gone.

.PARAMETER WorkerURL
The stable front door. Defaults to https://streamy-signal.thenightserver.workers.dev

.PARAMETER NoPublish
Skips telling the Worker about the new tunnel hostname (already-stable setups).

.EXAMPLE
.\dev\start-activity.ps1
.\dev\start-activity.ps1 -PublishToken 'a-long-random-secret'
.\dev\start-activity.ps1 -Stop
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
[string]$PublishToken = "devsecret",
    [int]$RelayPort = 8790,
[int]$BotPort = 8791,
    [int]$GatewayPort = 8799,
[string]$WorkerURL = "https://streamy-signal.thenightserver.workers.dev",
    [string]$AdminTokenFile = "",
[switch]$NoTunnel,
    [switch]$NoPublish,
[switch]$Stop,
    [switch]$SkipBuild,
[switch]$Hidden
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"

# Windows PowerShell 5.1 evaluates advanced-script ([CmdletBinding()]) parameter

# defaults before $PSScriptRoot is set, so any default that needs the script's

# folder has to be resolved here, in the body. $MyInvocation is a fallback for

# hosts that leave $PSScriptRoot empty.

$ScriptRoot = $PSScriptRoot
if (-not $ScriptRoot) { $ScriptRoot = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path }

if (-not $AdminTokenFile) {
$AdminTokenFile = Join-Path $ScriptRoot "secrets\tunnel-admin-token.txt"
}

$Site = Split-Path -Parent $ScriptRoot
$RunDir = Join-Path $ScriptRoot ".run"
$TunnelPidFile = Join-Path $RunDir "tunnel.pid"
$TunnelLog = Join-Path $RunDir "tunnel.log"
$TunnelErrLog = Join-Path $RunDir "tunnel.err.log"
$GatewayExe = Join-Path $Site "gateway\gateway.exe"

function Write-Section($text) {
Write-Host ""
Write-Host " $text" -ForegroundColor Cyan
}

function Get-PortOwner([int]$Port) {
try {
return Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort $Port -State Listen -ErrorAction Stop |
Select-Object -First 1 -ExpandProperty OwningProcess
} catch {
return $null
}
}

function Stop-PortOwner([int]$Port, [string]$Label) {
$owner = Get-PortOwner $Port
    if (-not $owner) {
        Write-Host "  $Label : port $Port already free" -ForegroundColor DarkGray
        return
    }
    try {
        $process = Get-Process -Id $owner -ErrorAction Stop
        Stop-Process -Id $owner -Force
        Write-Host "  $Label : stopped $($process.ProcessName) (pid $owner) on port $Port" -ForegroundColor Yellow
} catch {
Write-Host " $Label : could not stop pid $owner on port $Port" -ForegroundColor Red
}
}

function Read-DotEnv([string]$Path) {
    $values = @{}
    if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $Path)) { return $values }
    foreach ($line in Get-Content -LiteralPath $Path) {
        $trimmed = $line.Trim()
        if (-not $trimmed -or $trimmed.StartsWith("#")) { continue }
        $index = $trimmed.IndexOf("=")
        if ($index -le 0) { continue }
$key = $trimmed.Substring(0, $index).Trim()
        $value = $trimmed.Substring($index + 1).Trim()
if ($value.Length -ge 2 -and ($value.StartsWith('"') -or $value.StartsWith("'")) -and $value.EndsWith($value[0])) {
$value = $value.Substring(1, $value.Length - 2)
        }
        $values[$key] = $value
}
return $values
}

function Start-StackWindow([string]$Title, [string]$Directory, [string]$Command, [string]$PidFile) {
$inner = "`$Host.UI.RawUI.WindowTitle = '$Title'; Set-Location -LiteralPath '$Directory'; $Command"
    $encoded = [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::Unicode.GetBytes($inner))
$psArgs = @("-NoProfile", "-EncodedCommand", $encoded)
$style = "Normal"

# Gateway

One local port that serves the built viewer and proxies the two Activity
backends. It exists because the relay, bot and viewer must sit behind **one**
origin that Cloudflare can reach, while Discord only exposes two mapped paths.

```
https://<random>.trycloudflare.com/     (internal, republished automatically)
�"o�"?�"? /              -> viewer/dist      (Activity app, local checks)
�"o�"?�"? /v1/...        -> relay :8790      (WebSocket, prefix already stripped)
�"o�"?�"? /relay/...     -> relay :8790      (same routes, prefix preserved)
�"o�"?�"? /token         -> bot   :8791      (prefix already stripped)
�""�"?�"? /api/...       -> bot   :8791      (prefix preserved)
```

The tunnel hostname is not user-facing. `streamy-signal` (the signaling Worker)
is the stable front door: it proxies `/token` and the relay WebSocket to whatever
tunnel host the launcher last published, so the Developer Portal never changes.
The viewer itself is served from `https://streamy-viewer.pages.dev`.

Discord strips URL-mapping prefixes before forwarding, so a request to
`/.proxy/api/token` arrives as `/token` and `/.proxy/relay/v1/watch/<room>`
arrives as `/v1/watch/<room>`. Both the stripped and the prefixed paths are
handled, so the gateway works whatever the proxy does.

The desktop app never uses the gateway: it publishes to the relay
(`ws://127.0.0.1:8790` locally) and calls the bot (`http://127.0.0.1:8791`)
directly. Only the Activity inside Discord goes through the public tunnel.

## Build and run

```powershell
cd stream-site/gateway
go build -o gateway.exe .

# from another terminal, with the relay and bot already running:
.\gateway.exe -addr 127.0.0.1:8799 `
  -viewer ..\viewer\dist `
  -relay http://127.0.0.1:8790 `
  -bot   http://127.0.0.1:8791
```

Then point the tunnel at the gateway:

```powershell
cloudflared tunnel --url http://127.0.0.1:8799
```

`dev/start-activity.ps1` runs all four processes, publishes the tunnel host to
the Worker (`PUT /__tunnel`) and prints the stable portal values.

| Flag      | Default                 | Meaning                                                                    |
| --------- | ----------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-addr`   | `127.0.0.1:8799`        | Listen address. Keep it on loopback; the tunnel is the only public path.   |
| `-viewer` | `../viewer/dist`        | Built viewer directory. The gateway refuses to start without `index.html`. |
| `-relay`  | `http://127.0.0.1:8790` | Relay base URL.                                                            |
| `-bot`    | `http://127.0.0.1:8791` | Bot HTTP API base URL.                                                     |

`GET /healthz` returns the configured upstreams. Every request is logged with
method, path, status and duration, which is the quickest way to see what Discord
actually sent through a URL mapping.

## Notes

- WebSocket upgrades are proxied by `net/http/httputil`, so no extra headers or
  timeouts are needed here.
- `config.json` and `index.html` are served with `Cache-Control: no-store` so a
  redeploy is picked up on the next Activity launch; hashed Vite assets still
  cache normally.
- Unknown paths fall back to `index.html` so client-side routes keep working.
- This is a development and small-deployment convenience. For a real deployment
  put the viewer on Pages/static hosting and give the relay and bot their own
  hostnames (see `../DISCORD_ACTIVITY.md`).

# relay/

Small Go WebSocket relay for the Discord Activity path. It accepts one publisher
per room, caches SPS/PPS and the latest IDR, and fans encoded H.264 access units
and Opus packets out to every viewer.

```
Streamy app �"?�"?/v1/publish/<room>�"?�"?�-� relay �"?�"?/v1/watch/<room>�"?�"?�-� Activity viewers
```

The relay does not decode, transcode, or negotiate WebRTC. It forwards the
publisher's binary frames unchanged.

## Build and run

```bash
cd stream-site/relay
go build -o streamy-relay .
RELAY_PUBLISH_TOKEN='<long-random-secret>' ./streamy-relay -addr :8790 -max-viewers 200
```

| Flag / env                               | Default | Meaning                                          |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `-addr`                                  | `:8790` | HTTP listen address.                             |
| `-publish-token` / `RELAY_PUBLISH_TOKEN` | empty   | Publisher secret. Empty disables publisher auth. |
| `-max-viewers`                           | `200`   | Per-room viewer cap; `0` is unlimited.           |

`GET /healthz` returns `ok` for load balancers.

Run it at the host root. Publisher base URLs in Streamy are
`wss://relay.example.com`; the relay appends `/v1/publish/<room>`. The viewer
path is `wss://relay.example.com/v1/watch/<room>`. The relay also accepts
`/relay/v1/publish/<room>` and `/relay/v1/watch/<room>` for proxies that preserve
the Discord mapping prefix.

## TLS and reverse proxy

Activity browsers require `wss:`. Caddy handles upgrades automatically:

```caddyfile
relay.example.com {
    reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:8790
}
```

nginx needs the upgrade headers:

```nginx
location / {
    proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8790;
    proxy_http_version 1.1;
    proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
    proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
    proxy_read_timeout 300s;
}
```

## Protocol

See [`../PROTOCOL.md`](../PROTOCOL.md), section **Activity relay protocol �?" v1**.
Summary:

- First text frame is `{"v":1,"type":"hello","role":"publisher","token":"..."}`
  or `{"v":1,"type":"hello","role":"viewer"}`.
- Server replies `{"v":1,"type":"ready",...}` or an `error` then closes.
- Binary frames: 10-byte header `type(1) flags(1) timestamp(uint64 BE Unix ms)`
  followed by an Annex-B H.264 access unit (`0x01`) or a raw Opus packet
  (`0x02`). Flag `0x01` marks a keyframe.
- New viewers receive the cached keyframe immediately.
- `ping`/`pong` text keepalives; the server pings every 30 s.
- Close codes: `4001` publisher gone, `4002` room in use, `4003` room full,
  `4008` unauthorized. `4004` (slow consumer) is reserved: the relay no longer
  disconnects a viewer for being slow (see below), but clients still handle it.

## Limits and operations

- **Single instance.** Rooms live in memory. A restart drops streams, and there
  is no cross-instance routing.
- **Bandwidth.** Publisher ingress is about the stream bitrate; viewer egress is
  about `bitrate �- viewers`. The relay logs per-room `publisher_kbps` and
  `viewer_egress_kbps` every 10 seconds.
- **Slow viewers skip ahead.** Each viewer has a 64-message queue. If it fills,
  the queued backlog is dropped and the viewer resumes at the next keyframe, so
  it stays connected and close to the live edge instead of building up latency.
  The publisher is never blocked.
- **Viewers are unauthenticated.** The room ID (Discord channel ID) is the
  capability. Anyone who can reach the relay and knows the room can watch.
- **The relay sees all media.** Treat the VPS and publisher token as sensitive.

## Tests

```bash
cd stream-site/relay
go test ./...
```

The integration tests cover fan-out, the cached keyframe with parameter sets,
publisher auth rejection, room-in-use, the viewer cap, and the `4001` close when
the publisher leaves.

See [`../DISCORD_ACTIVITY.md`](../DISCORD_ACTIVITY.md) for the full deployment
and test plan.

func (p *ReverseProxy) handleUpgradeResponse(rw http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request, res *http.Response) {

func (s *Server) dropRoom(id string, r *room.Room) {

This is a real, severe bug (self-deadlock on r.mu) whenever a room becomes empty. In the user's Activity, after someone leaves, the room deadlocks, so later viewers hang forever → "Reconnecting". This is exactly the kind of discrepancy to fix.

Fix: add a method `Room.Empty() bool` that locks once and returns `publisher==nil && len(viewers)==0`, and use it in dropRoom. Or make Publisher/ViewerCount non-locking. Best: add `Empty()`:

```go
func (r *Room) Empty() bool {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	return r.publisher == nil && len(r.viewers) == 0
}
```

Then dropRoom:

```go
func (s *Server) dropRoom(id string, r *room.Room) {
	if !r.Empty() {
		return
	}
	s.mu.Lock()
	if s.rooms[id] == r {
		delete(s.rooms, id)
	}
	s.mu.Unlock()
}
```

155: func (r *Room) Publisher() *RelayClient {
156: r.mu.Lock()
157: defer r.mu.Unlock()
158: return r.publisher
159: }
160:
161: func (r *Room) AddPublisher(c *RelayClient) bool {
162: r.mu.Lock()
163: defer r.mu.Unlock()
164: if r.publisher != nil {
165: return false
166: }
167: r.publisher = c
168: return true
169: }
170:
171: func (r *Room) RemovePublisher(c *RelayClient) {
172: r.mu.Lock()
173: if r.publisher == c {
174: r.publisher = nil
175: }
176: r.mu.Unlock()
177: }
178:
179: func (r *Room) AddViewer(c *RelayClient, maxViewers int) bool {
180: r.mu.Lock()
181: defer r.mu.Unlock()
182: if maxViewers > 0 && len(r.viewers) >= maxViewers {
183: return false
184: }
185: r.viewers[c] = struct{}{}
186: return true
187: }
188:
189: func (r *Room) RemoveViewer(c *RelayClient) {
190: r.mu.Lock()
191: delete(r.viewers, c)
192: r.mu.Unlock()
193: }
194:
195: func (r *Room) ViewerCount() int {
196: r.mu.Lock()
197: defer r.mu.Unlock()
198: return len(r.viewers)
199: }
200:
201: // Empty reports whether the room holds no publisher and no viewers. It takes
202: // the lock itself: dropRoom must not call Publisher or ViewerCount while
203: // already holding r.mu, or the room deadlocks and every later viewer for the
204: // same room hangs before it can be accepted.
205: func (r *Room) Empty() bool {
206: r.mu.Lock()
207: defer r.mu.Unlock()
208: return r.publisher == nil && len(r.viewers) == 0
209: }
210:
211: func (r *Room) Publish(frame protocol.MediaFrame, encoded []byte) {
212: r.bytesIn.Add(uint64(len(encoded)))
213:
214: r.mu.Lock()
215: keyframe := false
216: if frame.Kind == protocol.MediaVideo {
217: info := inspectH264(frame.Payload)
218: if info.sps != nil {
219: r.sps = info.sps
220: }
221: if info.pps != nil {
222: r.pps = info.pps
223: }
224: keyframe = info.hasIDR
225: if keyframe {
226: r.keyframe = append(r.keyframe[:0], frame.Payload...)
227: r.keyframeStamp = frame.Timestamp
228: }
229: }
230: viewers := make([]*RelayClient, 0, len(r.viewers))
231: for viewer := range r.viewers {
232: viewers = append(viewers, viewer)
233: }
234: r.mu.Unlock()
235:
236: for \_, viewer := range viewers {
237: if viewer.TrySendMedia(Outbound{MessageType: websocket.BinaryMessage, Data: encoded}, frame.Kind == protocol.MediaVideo, keyframe) {
238: r.bytesOut.Add(uint64(len(encoded)))
239: }
240: }
241: }
242:
243: func (r *Room) SendCachedKeyframe(c *RelayClient, now uint64) {
244: r.mu.Lock()
245: keyframe := append([]byte(nil), r.keyframe...)
246: sps := append([]byte(nil), r.sps...)
247: pps := append([]byte(nil), r.pps...)
248: r.mu.Unlock()
249: if len(keyframe) == 0 {
250: return
251: }
252: keyframe = addMissingParameterSets(keyframe, sps, pps)
253: encoded := protocol.EncodeMediaFrame(protocol.MediaVideo, protocol.FlagKeyframe, now, keyframe)
254: if c.TrySendMedia(Outbound{MessageType: websocket.BinaryMessage, Data: encoded}, true, true) {
255: r.bytesOut.Add(uint64(len(encoded)))
256: }
257: }
258:
259: func (r *Room) CloseViewers(code int, reason string) {
260: r.mu.Lock()
261: viewers := make([]*RelayClient, 0, len(r.viewers))
262: for viewer := range r.viewers {
263: viewers = append(viewers, viewer)
264: }
265: r.viewers = make(map[*RelayClient]struct{})
266: r.mu.Unlock()
267: for _, viewer := range viewers {
268: viewer.SendJSON(map[string]any{
269: "v": protocol.ProtocolVersion, "type": "error", "code": "publisher-gone", "message": reason,
270: })
271: viewer.Close(code, reason)
272: }
273: }
274:
275: func (r \*Room) Stats() (viewers int, bytesIn, bytesOut uint64) {
276: return r.ViewerCount(), r.bytesIn.Swap(0), r.bytesOut.Swap(0)
277: }
278:
279: type h264Info struct {
280: sps []byte
281: pps []byte
282: hasIDR bool
283: }
284:
285: // inspectH264 reads one Annex-B access unit. The publisher hands the relay
286: // ffmpeg's Annex-B output (start codes, not 4-byte length prefixes), so the NAL
287: // header is the byte after the start code. Parsing it as a length prefix made
288: // every frame look like a giant unknown NAL: no keyframe was ever cached and a
289: // viewer joining mid-stream got deltas it could not decode.
290: func inspectH264(payload []byte) h264Info {
291: var info h264Info
292: for _, nal := range splitAnnexB(payload) {
293: if len(nal) == 0 {
294: continue
295: }
296: switch nal[0] & 0x1F {
297: case 7: // SPS
298: info.sps = append([]byte{0, 0, 0, 1}, nal...)
299: case 8: // PPS
300: info.pps = append([]byte{0, 0, 0, 1}, nal...)
301: case 5: // IDR
302: info.hasIDR = true
303: }
304: }
305: return info
306: }
307:
308: // splitAnnexB returns the NAL units of an Annex-B buffer without their start
309: // codes.
310: func splitAnnexB(data []byte) [][]byte {
311: var nals [][]byte
312: start := -1
313: for i := 0; i+2 < len(data); {
314: startCode := 0
315: switch {
316: case data[i] == 0 && data[i+1] == 0 && data[i+2] == 1:
317: startCode = 3
318: case i+3 < len(data) && data[i] == 0 && data[i+1] == 0 && data[i+2] == 0 && data[i+3] == 1:
319: startCode = 4
320: }
321: if startCode == 0 {
322: i++
323: continue
324: }
325: if start >= 0 {
326: nals = append(nals, data[start:i])
327: }
328: start = i + startCode
329: i = start
330: }
331: if start >= 0 && start < len(data) {
332: nals = append(nals, data[start:])
333: }
334: return nals
335: }
336:
337: // addMissingParameterSets makes a cached keyframe self-contained without
338: // repeating parameter sets that it already carries.
339: func addMissingParameterSets(payload []byte, sps, pps []byte) []byte {
340: info := inspectH264(payload)
341: var prefix []byte
342: if info.sps == nil && len(sps) > 0 {
343: prefix = append(prefix, sps...)
344: }
345: if info.pps == nil && len(pps) > 0 {
346: prefix = append(prefix, pps...)
347: }
348: if len(prefix) == 0 {
349: return payload
350: }
351: result := make([]byte, 0, len(prefix)+len(payload))
352: result = append(result, prefix...)
353: result = append(result, payload...)
354: return result
355: }

62: s.mu.Lock()
63: defer s.mu.Unlock()

67: s.rooms[id] = r

74: return
75: }

78: delete(s.rooms, id)

91: func (s *Server) handle(w http.ResponseWriter, req *http.Request, role string) {
92: roomID := strings.TrimSpace(req.PathValue("room"))
93: if !validRoomID(roomID) {
94: http.Error(w, "invalid room id", http.StatusBadRequest)
95: return
96: }
97: conn, err := s.upgrader.Upgrade(w, req, nil)
98: if err != nil {
99: return
100: }
101: conn.SetReadLimit(protocol.MaxMediaBytes + protocol.MediaHeaderSize)
102: defer conn.Close()
103:
104: client := &room.RelayClient{
105: Conn: conn,
106: Role: role,
107: Send: make(chan room.Outbound, room.ViewerQueueDepth),
108: Done: make(chan struct{}),
109: }
110:
111: hello, err := readHello(conn)
112: if err != nil {
113: writeJSONNow(conn, errorMessage("bad-message", err.Error()))
114: conn.WriteControl(websocket.CloseMessage,
115: websocket.FormatCloseMessage(websocket.ClosePolicyViolation, "bad hello"),
116: time.Now().Add(time.Second))
117: return
118: }
119: if hello.Version != protocol.ProtocolVersion {
120: writeJSONNow(conn, errorMessage("unsupported-version", "relay protocol version is 1"))
121: client.Close(websocket.CloseProtocolError, "unsupported version")
122: return
123: }
124: if hello.Role != role {
125: writeJSONNow(conn, errorMessage("bad-message", "role does not match endpoint"))
126: client.Close(websocket.ClosePolicyViolation, "wrong role")
127: return
128: }
129:
130: conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(protocol.ReadDeadline))
131: conn.SetPongHandler(func(string) error {
132: return conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(protocol.ReadDeadline))
133: })
134:
135: switch role {
136: case "publisher":
137: if s.publishTok != "" && !constantTimeEqual(hello.Token, s.publishTok) {
138: writeJSONNow(conn, errorMessage("unauthorized", "invalid publisher token"))
139: client.Close(protocol.CloseUnauthorized, "unauthorized")
140: return
141: }
142: r := s.getRoom(roomID)
143: client.Room = r
144: if !r.AddPublisher(client) {
145: writeJSONNow(conn, errorMessage("room-in-use", "a publisher is already connected"))
146: client.Close(protocol.CloseRoomInUse, "room in use")
147: s.dropRoom(roomID, r)
148: return
149: }
150: defer func() {
151: r.RemovePublisher(client)
152: r.CloseViewers(protocol.CloseHostGone, "publisher disconnected")
153: s.dropRoom(roomID, r)
154: s.logger.Info("publisher left", "room", roomID)
155: }()
156: client.SendJSON(map[string]any{
157: "v": protocol.ProtocolVersion, "type": "ready", "room": roomID, "role": "publisher",
158: })
159: s.logger.Info("publisher connected", "room", roomID, "viewers", r.ViewerCount())
160:
161: case "viewer":
162: r := s.getRoom(roomID)
163: client.Room = r
164: if !r.AddViewer(client, s.maxViewers) {
165: writeJSONNow(conn, errorMessage("room-full", "viewer limit reached"))
166: client.Close(protocol.CloseRoomFull, "room full")
167: s.dropRoom(roomID, r)
168: return
169: }
170: defer func() {
171: r.RemoveViewer(client)
172: s.dropRoom(roomID, r)
173: s.logger.Debug("viewer left", "room", roomID, "viewers", r.ViewerCount())
174: }()
175: client.SendJSON(map[string]any{
176: "v": protocol.ProtocolVersion, "type": "ready", "room": roomID, "role": "viewer",
177: })
178: r.SendCachedKeyframe(client, uint64(time.Now().UnixMilli()))
179: s.logger.Info("viewer connected", "room", roomID, "viewers", r.ViewerCount())
180: }
181:
182: go client.Writer()
183: s.readLoop(client)
184: }
185:
186: func (s *Server) readLoop(c \*room.RelayClient) {
187: defer c.Close(websocket.CloseNormalClosure, "leaving")
188: for {
189: messageType, data, err := c.Conn.ReadMessage()
190: if err != nil {
191: return
192: }
193: c.Conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(protocol.ReadDeadline))
194: if messageType == websocket.TextMessage {
195: var control room.ControlMessage
196: if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &control); err != nil {
197: continue
198: }
199: if control.Type == "ping" {
200: c.SendJSON(map[string]any{"v": protocol.ProtocolVersion, "type": "pong", "t": control.Time})
201: }
202: continue
203: }
204: if messageType != websocket.BinaryMessage || c.Role != "publisher" {
205: continue
206: }
207: frame, err := protocol.ParseMediaFrame(data)
208: if err != nil || len(frame.Payload) == 0 {
209: continue
210: }
211: c.Room.Publish(frame, data)
212: }
213: }

187: defer c.Close(websocket.CloseNormalClosure, "leaving")
188: for {
189: messageType, data, err := c.Conn.ReadMessage()
190: if err != nil {

193: c.Conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(protocol.ReadDeadline))
194: if messageType == websocket.TextMessage {
195: var control room.ControlMessage
196: if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &control); err != nil {
197: continue
198: }
199: if control.Type == "ping" {
200: c.SendJSON(map[string]any{"v": protocol.ProtocolVersion, "type": "pong", "t": control.Time})
201: }
202: continue
203: }
204: if messageType != websocket.BinaryMessage || c.Role != "publisher" {
205: continue
206: }
207: frame, err := protocol.ParseMediaFrame(data)
208: if err != nil || len(frame.Payload) == 0 {
209: continue
210: }
211: c.Room.Publish(frame, data)
212: }
213: }

    "golang.org/x/sys/windows"

    "streamy/internal/signal"

func unprotect(protected []byte) ([]byte, error) {
if len(protected) == 0 {
return nil, nil
}
input := windows.DataBlob{Size: uint32(len(protected)), Data: &protected[0]}
var output windows.DataBlob
if err := windows.CryptUnprotectData(&input, nil, nil, 0, nil, windows.CRYPTPROTECT_UI_FORBIDDEN, &output); err != nil {
return nil, err
}
defer windows.LocalFree(windows.Handle(uintptr(unsafe.Pointer(output.Data))))
result := make([]byte, output.Size)
copy(result, unsafe.Slice((\*byte)(unsafe.Pointer(output.Data)), output.Size))
return result, nil
}

/\*\*

- Discord Activity bootstrap.
-
- An Activity page is served from discordsays.com inside an iframe. Discord
- adds `frame_id` to the query string, and the only backend URLs that work are
- the relative `/.proxy/...` mappings configured in the Developer Portal.
  \*/
  export function isActivity() {
  const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
  return params.has("frame_id") || /(^|\.)discordsays\.com$/i.test(location.hostname);
  }

/\*\*

- Runs the full embedded-app handshake and returns the room identity.
- Throws an Error with a user-readable message on failure.
  \*/
  export async function bootstrapActivity(config) {
  if (!isActivity()) return null;

const clientId = config?.discordClientID;
if (!clientId) throw new Error("config.json has no discordClientID.");

let DiscordSDK;
try {
({ DiscordSDK } = await import("@discord/embedded-app-sdk"));
} catch (error) {
throw new Error(`The Discord Activity SDK failed to load: ${messageOf(error)}`);
}

const sdk = new DiscordSDK(clientId);
await sdk.ready();

let code;
try {
const authorization = await sdk.commands.authorize({
client_id: clientId,
response_type: "code",
state: "streamy",
prompt: "none",
scope: ["identify", "guilds"],
});
code = authorization.code;
} catch (error) {
throw new Error(`Discord authorization was cancelled or failed: ${messageOf(error)}`);
}
if (!code) throw new Error("Discord did not return an authorization code.");

// This relative path is rewritten by Discord's proxy. Never use the bot's
// absolute hostname here: the Activity iframe cannot reach it directly.
// Discord strips the mapping prefix, so `/.proxy/api/token` reaches the bot
// as `/token`; the bot accepts both paths.
const tokenURL = config?.tokenURL || "/.proxy/api/token";
if (!tokenURL.startsWith("/.proxy/")) {
throw new Error("config.json tokenURL must be a relative /.proxy/ path inside Discord.");
}
const response = await fetch(tokenURL, {
method: "POST",
headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
body: JSON.stringify({ code }),
});
if (!response.ok) {
const detail = await response.text().catch(() => "");
throw new Error(`The token exchange failed (HTTP ${response.status}). ${detail}`.trim());
}

const token = await response.json();
if (!token.access_token) throw new Error("The token exchange returned no access_token.");

try {
await sdk.commands.authenticate({ access_token: token.access_token });
} catch (error) {
throw new Error(`Discord authentication failed: ${messageOf(error)}`);
}

const room = sdk.channelId || sdk.instanceId;
if (!room) throw new Error("Discord did not provide a channel or instance ID.");

return {
sdk,
room: String(room),
channelId: sdk.channelId ? String(sdk.channelId) : "",
instanceId: sdk.instanceId ? String(sdk.instanceId) : "",
accessToken: token.access_token,
};
}

function messageOf(error) {
return error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
}

164: // runCloudflared starts cloudflared tunnel pointing to the gateway,
165: // parses the tunnel URL from stdout, and registers it with the bot.
166: func runCloudflared(ctx context.Context, logger *slog.Logger, bin, extraArgs, gatewayAddr string, botSrv *bot.Bot) error {
167: // Parse gateway address to get port
168: *, port, err := net.SplitHostPort(gatewayAddr)
169: if err != nil {
170: return fmt.Errorf("invalid gateway address %q: %w", gatewayAddr, err)
171: }
172:
173: // Build cloudflared command
174: args := []string{"tunnel", "--url", "http://localhost:" + port, "--no-autoupdate"}
175: if extraArgs != "" {
176: // Simple split on spaces - good enough for our use case
177: for \_, arg := range splitArgs(extraArgs) {
178: args = append(args, arg)
179: }
180: }
181:
182: cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, bin, args...)
183: cmd.Stdout = nil // We'll capture via pipe
184: cmd.Stderr = nil
185:
186: stdout, err := cmd.StdoutPipe()
187: if err != nil {
188: return fmt.Errorf("stdout pipe: %w", err)
189: }
190: stderr, err := cmd.StderrPipe()
191: if err != nil {
192: return fmt.Errorf("stderr pipe: %w", err)
193: }
194:
195: if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
196: return fmt.Errorf("start cloudflared: %w", err)
197: }
198:
199: logger.Info("cloudflared started", "bin", bin, "url", "http://localhost:"+port)
200:
201: // Regex to match cloudflared tunnel URL: https://<subdomain>.trycloudflare.com
202: // or https://<subdomain>.cloudflareaccess.com (for named tunnels)
203: urlRegex := regexp.MustCompile(`https://[a-zA-Z0-9\-]+\.(trycloudflare\.com|cloudflareaccess\.com)`)
204:
205: // Read stdout and stderr to find the tunnel URL
206: done := make(chan struct{})
207: go func() {
208: defer close(done)
209: scanner := bufio.NewScanner(io.MultiReader(stdout, stderr))
210: for scanner.Scan() {
211: line := scanner.Text()
212: logger.Debug("cloudflared", "output", line)
213: if matches := urlRegex.FindStringSubmatch(line); len(matches) > 0 {
214: tunnelURL := matches[0]
215: // Extract just the host part (without https://)
216: host := strings.TrimPrefix(tunnelURL, "https://")
217: logger.Info("cloudflared tunnel ready", "url", tunnelURL)
218: if err := botSrv.SetTunnelURL(host); err != nil {
219: logger.Error("failed to register tunnel with bot", "error", err)
220: }
221: }
222: }
223: if err := scanner.Err(); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
224: logger.Error("cloudflared output scanner error", "error", err)
225: }
226: }()
227:
228: // Wait for command to finish
229: err = cmd.Wait()
230: <-done
231:
232: // Clean up tunnel registration on exit
233: botSrv.DeleteTunnel()
234:
235: return err
236: }

238: // splitArgs splits a string on spaces, respecting quoted strings.
239: func splitArgs(s string) []string {
240: var args []string
241: var current strings.Builder
242: inQuote := false
243: quoteChar := byte(0)
244: for i := 0; i < len(s); i++ {
245: c := s[i]
246: if (c == '"' || c == '\'') && !inQuote {
247: inQuote = true
248: quoteChar = c
249: } else if c == quoteChar && inQuote {
250: inQuote = false
251: quoteChar = 0
252: } else if c == ' ' && !inQuote {
253: if current.Len() > 0 {
254: args = append(args, current.String())
255: current.Reset()
256: }
257: } else {
258: current.WriteByte(c)
259: }
260: }
261: if current.Len() > 0 {
262: args = append(args, current.String())
263: }
264: return args
265: }

});

}

}

// Lets the local start script publish "this is the tunnel serving the relay
// right now" without anyone touching the Developer Portal. The tunnel hostname
// is the only thing that changes between runs, and it is stored in the Lobby
// Durable Object so lookups are immediately consistent.
async function handleTunnelAdmin(request, env) {
const expected = env.TUNNEL_ADMIN_TOKEN || "";
if (!expected) return jsonResponse({ error: "admin-not-configured" }, 503);
const provided = (request.headers.get("authorization") || "").replace(/^Bearer\s+/i, "");
if (!constantTimeEqual(provided, expected)) return jsonResponse({ error: "unauthorized" }, 401);

const lobby = env.LOBBY.get(env.LOBBY.idFromName("public"));
if (request.method === "GET") {
const response = await lobby.fetch("https://lobby/tunnel");
return jsonResponse(await response.json(), 200, { "cache-control": "no-store" });
}
if (request.method === "PUT") {
const response = await lobby.fetch("https://lobby/tunnel", {
method: "PUT",
headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
body: await request.text(),
});
if (response.ok) return jsonResponse({ ok: true }, 200);
return jsonResponse({ error: "invalid-host" }, response.status);
}
if (request.method === "DELETE") {
await lobby.fetch("https://lobby/tunnel", { method: "DELETE" });
return jsonResponse({ ok: true }, 200);
}
return jsonResponse({ error: "method-not-allowed" }, 405, { allow: "GET, PUT, DELETE" });
}

function constantTimeEqual(left, right) {
if (typeof left !== "string" || typeof right !== "string" || left.length !== right.length) return false;
let diff = 0;
for (let index = 0; index < left.length; index += 1) {
diff |= left.charCodeAt(index) ^ right.charCodeAt(index);
