// Stable front door for the self-hosted relay and bot.
//
// Discord's Activity proxy sends /.proxy/api/_ and /.proxy/relay/_ here, and we
// forward them to whichever Cloudflare tunnel is currently pointed at the
// user's machine. The tunnel hostname is looked up from KV on every request so
// restarting the local stack never requires touching the Developer Portal.

const EXACT_PATHS = new Set(["/token", "/api/token"]);

const PATH_PREFIXES = ["/v1/watch/", "/v1/publish/", "/relay/", "/relay"];

export function isTunnelPath(pathname) {
if (EXACT_PATHS.has(pathname)) return true;
return PATH_PREFIXES.some((prefix) => pathname === prefix || pathname.startsWith(prefix.endsWith("/") ? prefix : `${prefix}/`));
}

function tunnelOrigin(host) {
const trimmed = String(host || "").trim().replace(/\/+$/, "");
  if (!trimmed) return "";
  if (/^https?:\/\//i.test(trimmed)) return trimmed;
  if (/^[a-z0-9.-]+(:\d+)?$/i.test(trimmed)) return `https://${trimmed}`;
return "";
}

async function currentHost(env) {
if (env.LOBBY) {
try {
const lobby = env.LOBBY.get(env.LOBBY.idFromName("public"));
const response = await lobby.fetch("https://lobby/tunnel");
if (response.ok) {
const data = await response.json();
if (data && typeof data.host === "string" && data.host) return data.host;
}
} catch {
// Fall through to the static value so local dev keeps working.
}
}
return env.TUNNEL_HOST || "";
}

export async function proxyToTunnel(request, env, url) {
const origin = tunnelOrigin(await currentHost(env));
if (!origin) {
return new Response(JSON.stringify({ error: "relay-offline" }), {
status: 503,
headers: { "content-type": "application/json", "cache-control": "no-store" },
});
}
let pathname = url.pathname;

headers.set("x-forwarded-host", url.host);
headers.set("x-forwarded-proto", url.protocol.replace(":", ""));
headers.delete("host");

method: request.method,
headers,
redirect: "manual",

}

45: func (c *RelayClient) trySend(message Outbound) bool {
46: select {
47: case c.Send <- message:
48: return true
49: default:
50: return false
51: }
52: }

54: func (c *RelayClient) TrySendMedia(message Outbound, video, keyframe bool) bool {
55: if video {
56: if c.needsKeyframe.Load() && !keyframe {
57: return false
58: }
59: if keyframe {
60: c.needsKeyframe.Store(false)
61: }
62: }
63: select {
64: case c.Send <- message:
65: return true
66: default:
67: }
68:
69: // Drop backlog and wait for keyframe
70: for {
71: select {
72: case <-c.Send:
73: default:
74: if !keyframe {
75: c.needsKeyframe.Store(true)
76: }
77: if video && !keyframe {
78: return false
79: }
80: select {
81: case c.Send <- message:
82: return true
83: default:
84: return false
85: }
86: }
87: }
88: }

90: func (c *RelayClient) SendJSON(v any) bool {
91: data, err := json.Marshal(v)
92: if err != nil {
93: return false
94: }
95: return c.trySend(Outbound{MessageType: websocket.TextMessage, Data: data})
96: }

98: func (c *RelayClient) Close(code int, reason string) {
99: c.closeOnce.Do(func() {
100: close(c.Done)
101: c.Conn.WriteControl(websocket.CloseMessage,
102: websocket.FormatCloseMessage(code, reason),
103: time.Now().Add(5*time.Second))
104: c.Conn.Close()
105: })
106: }
107:
108: func (c *RelayClient) Writer() {
109: ping := time.NewTicker(PingInterval)
110: defer ping.Stop()
111: for {
112: select {
113: case <-c.Done:
114: return
115: case message := <-c.Send:
116: c.Conn.SetWriteDeadline(time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second))
117: if err := c.Conn.WriteMessage(message.MessageType, message.Data); err != nil {
118: return
119: }
120: case <-ping.C:
121: if err := c.Conn.WriteControl(websocket.PingMessage, nil, time.Now().Add(10*time.Second)); err != nil {
122: return
123: }
124: }
125: }
126: }

162: r.mu.Lock()

167: r.publisher = c

180: r.mu.Lock()
181: defer r.mu.Unlock()
182: if maxViewers > 0 && len(r.viewers) >= maxViewers {
183: return false
184: }

190: r.mu.Lock()

192: r.mu.Unlock()
193: }

195: func (r *Room) ViewerCount() int {
196: r.mu.Lock()
197: defer r.mu.Unlock()
198: return len(r.viewers)
199: }
200:
201: // Empty reports whether the room holds no publisher and no viewers. It takes
202: // the lock itself: dropRoom must not call Publisher or ViewerCount while
203: // already holding r.mu, or the room deadlocks and every later viewer for the
204: // same room hangs before it can be accepted.
205: func (r *Room) Empty() bool {
206: r.mu.Lock()
207: defer r.mu.Unlock()
208: return r.publisher == nil && len(r.viewers) == 0
209: }

211: func (r *Room) Publish(frame protocol.MediaFrame, encoded []byte) {
212: r.bytesIn.Add(uint64(len(encoded)))
213:
214: r.mu.Lock()
215: keyframe := false
216: if frame.Kind == protocol.MediaVideo {
217: info := inspectH264(frame.Payload)
218: if info.sps != nil {
219: r.sps = info.sps
220: }
221: if info.pps != nil {
222: r.pps = info.pps
223: }
224: keyframe = info.hasIDR
225: if keyframe {
226: r.keyframe = append(r.keyframe[:0], frame.Payload...)
227: r.keyframeStamp = frame.Timestamp
228: }
229: }
230: viewers := make([]*RelayClient, 0, len(r.viewers))
231: for viewer := range r.viewers {
232: viewers = append(viewers, viewer)
233: }
234: r.mu.Unlock()
235:
236: for \_, viewer := range viewers {
237: if viewer.TrySendMedia(Outbound{MessageType: websocket.BinaryMessage, Data: encoded}, frame.Kind == protocol.MediaVideo, keyframe) {
238: r.bytesOut.Add(uint64(len(encoded)))
239: }
240: }
241: }

243: func (r *Room) SendCachedKeyframe(c *RelayClient, now uint64) {
244: r.mu.Lock()
245: keyframe := append([]byte(nil), r.keyframe...)
246: sps := append([]byte(nil), r.sps...)
247: pps := append([]byte(nil), r.pps...)
248: r.mu.Unlock()
249: if len(keyframe) == 0 {
250: return
251: }
252: keyframe = addMissingParameterSets(keyframe, sps, pps)
253: encoded := protocol.EncodeMediaFrame(protocol.MediaVideo, protocol.FlagKeyframe, now, keyframe)
254: if c.TrySendMedia(Outbound{MessageType: websocket.BinaryMessage, Data: encoded}, true, true) {
255: r.bytesOut.Add(uint64(len(encoded)))
256: }
257: }

259: func (r *Room) CloseViewers(code int, reason string) {
260: r.mu.Lock()
261: viewers := make([]*RelayClient, 0, len(r.viewers))
262: for viewer := range r.viewers {
263: viewers = append(viewers, viewer)
264: }
265: r.viewers = make(map[*RelayClient]struct{})
266: r.mu.Unlock()
267: for _, viewer := range viewers {
268: viewer.SendJSON(map[string]any{
269: "v": protocol.ProtocolVersion, "type": "error", "code": "publisher-gone", "message": reason,
270: })
271: viewer.Close(code, reason)
272: }
273: }

276: return r.ViewerCount(), r.bytesIn.Swap(0), r.bytesOut.Swap(0)
277: }

279: type h264Info struct {
280: sps []byte
281: pps []byte
282: hasIDR bool
283: }
284:
285: // inspectH264 reads one Annex-B access unit. The publisher hands the relay
286: // ffmpeg's Annex-B output (start codes, not 4-byte length prefixes), so the NAL
287: // header is the byte after the start code. Parsing it as a length prefix made
288: // every frame look like a giant unknown NAL: no keyframe was ever cached and a
289: // viewer joining mid-stream got deltas it could not decode.
290: func inspectH264(payload []byte) h264Info {
291: var info h264Info
292: for _, nal := range splitAnnexB(payload) {
293: if len(nal) == 0 {
294: continue
295: }
296: switch nal[0] & 0x1F {
297: case 7: // SPS
298: info.sps = append([]byte{0, 0, 0, 1}, nal...)
299: case 8: // PPS
300: info.pps = append([]byte{0, 0, 0, 1}, nal...)
301: case 5: // IDR
302: info.hasIDR = true
303: }
304: }
305: return info
306: }
307:
308: // splitAnnexB returns the NAL units of an Annex-B buffer without their start
309: // codes.
310: func splitAnnexB(data []byte) [][]byte {
311: var nals [][]byte
312: start := -1
313: for i := 0; i+2 < len(data); {
314: startCode := 0
315: switch {
316: case data[i] == 0 && data[i+1] == 0 && data[i+2] == 1:
317: startCode = 3
318: case i+3 < len(data) && data[i] == 0 && data[i+1] == 0 && data[i+2] == 0 && data[i+3] == 1:
319: startCode = 4
320: }
321: if startCode == 0 {
322: i++
323: continue
324: }
325: if start >= 0 {
326: nals = append(nals, data[start:i])
327: }
328: start = i + startCode
329: i = start
330: }
331: if start >= 0 && start < len(data) {
332: nals = append(nals, data[start:])
333: }
334: return nals
335: }
336:
337: // addMissingParameterSets makes a cached keyframe self-contained without
338: // repeating parameter sets that it already carries.
339: func addMissingParameterSets(payload []byte, sps, pps []byte) []byte {
340: info := inspectH264(payload)
341: var prefix []byte
342: if info.sps == nil && len(sps) > 0 {
343: prefix = append(prefix, sps...)
344: }
345: if info.pps == nil && len(pps) > 0 {
346: prefix = append(prefix, pps...)
347: }
348: if len(prefix) == 0 {
349: return payload
350: }
351: result := make([]byte, 0, len(prefix)+len(payload))
352: result = append(result, prefix...)
353: result = append(result, payload...)
354: return result
355: }

func (s *Server) joinRoom(id string, join func(*room.Room) bool) (*room.Room, bool) {

Black screen few seconds then still image: The first frame is drawn only when due; after ~120ms. But if it takes a few seconds, maybe the decoder output isn't decoded because the first chunk lacks SPS/PPS? The cached keyframe may not include SPS/PPS if publisher's cached keyframe was from an earlier stream and sps/pps stored separately; `SendCachedKeyframe` adds missing parameter sets. If the cached keyframe has them, OK.

Then subsequent deltas should decode. If they don't because `this.awaitingKeyframe` gets set true due to `late > 1500`, then resetVideo and wait for keyframe; keyframe interval config is 1 second (`keyframeSeconds: 1`), so it should resume quickly. Freezing permanently suggests either the publisher stopped sending after the viewer joined (but bandwidth shows 6 Mbps egress), or the viewer's decode pipeline errors and falls back, or the `frameQueue` logic drops everything.

Wait, bandwidth egress matches publisher, so frames are being sent to the WebSocket; the browser receives them. But are they being delivered to the page? Cloudflare tunnel is fine.

Could the Activity viewer's WebSocket buffer be flooded and the main thread can't keep up? 6 Mbps at 60fps ~ 12.5KB/frame; should be fine. But cloudflared/tunnel + Worker maybe adds latency. Still.

Could there be an issue with the timestamp on the cached keyframe: server sends cached keyframe with timestamp = server `now` at join. Then live publisher frames may have timestamps that are _older_ than that cached keyframe (because the keyframe was cached earlier and its payload re-stamped with current time, while live frames carry their original capture time, which could be slightly before `now`). The cached keyframe gets shown (timestamp 0), then live frames also timestamp 0 or increasing from 0. If live frames are older than the cached keyframe's fake timestamp, `encode` clamps all to 0, causing decoder timestamp collisions and only first frame decoded.

But `receiveVideo` has `if (timestamp < this.lastVideoTimestamp - 1000)` reset threshold. If live timestamps are only ~<1000ms older, no reset. So the clock origin could be ahead.
